newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds set to consolidate after Monday's advance.
newsitem.headline: Bunds set to consolidate after Monday's advance.

text.p: The surging Bund market looked set to take a breather on Tuesday after setting fresh contract highs late in the day on Monday.

Traders said the early focus is on German employment data for June, but they expect the figures will have little impact on German debt which has already factored in continued high unemployment for at least the rest of this year.
The market has already factored in a moderate decrease in joblessness during the month of around 30,000.
At 0712 GMT, the DTB Bund future was down seven basis points at 102.76, well off Monday's high of 102.92.
The cash 10-year benchmark Bund stood at 103.31 in early trade compared with 103.33 on Monday. The yield was 5.55 percent.
Traders said the contract looks well supported, some saying they see it now targeting 103.15.
Despite Monday's strong advance, Bunds were unable to climb much against Treasuries and the spread stood at 82 basis points during the morning here.
